transcript:
Header:
- Date/Time: 2025-05-20 16:00 PDT
- Duration: ~60 minutes
- Attendees: Jared (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Samir (Atlas PM), Lena (Atlas ML Eng), Carlos (Atlas Security)

Summary: Weekly POC check-in focused on quality/regression observed after last model patch. Short demo of examples and discussion about prompt-level scoring and guardrails. Some cross-talk and a couple of audio dropouts.

00:00 Jared: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we got about an hour on the calendar, happy to run through the quality diffs you flagged last week and go through the prompt set updates.
00:12 Samir: Yeah thanks Jared, this is Samir, we've seen a regression in the billing workflows, like the model started hallucinating chargeback reasons, which is new.
00:20 Maya: hi Samir, can you show one or two canonical examples? we pulled the logs and tried to reproduce locally but wanted your examples as ground truth.
00:31 Lena: sure, uh here's a sample, when asked why a charge was declined the response suggested "insufficient funds" followed by a random policy link, which we don't have. so that's inconsistency with our expected response set.
00:44 Jared: mm-hmm, ok. quick context — last week we upgraded to model v2.3-quant and also applied a more aggressive prompt compression step in the pipeline, so there are two variables.
00:58 Samir: right, and we're trying to understand if it's the quantized weights or the prompt template change.
01:08 Maya: we ran A/B locally and didn't reproduce large drift on our small test harness, but we did see lower confidence scores on some long-tail prompts; could be a tokenizer edge or prompt truncation with the compression.
01:22 Carlos: just to add a security angle, any change to prompt handling that logs PII or customer data differently is a big deal for us. what's Redwood's retention policy for prompt logs?
01:33 Jared: good question Carlos — Maya will share the SOC2 docs and the data flow diagram after this call, and we can annotate what fields we redact. by default we retain minimal request logs for 30 days in the hosted flow, but for Dedicated/Private you can change retention and KMS.
01:50 Lena: ok thanks. back to quality, we made a small scoring rubric — we grade on factual accuracy, policy conformity, and formatting. the regression is mostly on factual accuracy and a weird added link.
02:05 Maya: can you paste the exact prompt?
02:10 Samir: yup, "Why was charge #12345 declined on 2025-04-30?" then we map expected tokens to a set: [insufficient_funds, expired_card, cc_blocked_by_bank] — the model returned something like 'payment declined due to merchant policy - see merchant.com/policy/xyz' which is a hallucinated merchant link.
02:32 Jared: got it. two things we want to test: 1) run the prompt through the older v2.2 build to confirm regression, 2) try the same prompt without the compression step.
02:45 Maya: we also suggested a guardrail: post-process rule to disallow external-looking URLs in billing responses and prefer enumerated reasons from the allowed taxonomy. simple deterministic patch.
02:58 Samir: that sounds promising, yes. but we worry about masking legitimate links if they legitimately exist. not common in billing though.
03:08 Maya: right, rule would be high-precision: if response includes a domain-looking token and the confidence < 0.7 then redact and return taxonomy instead.
03:20 Lena: can we get the confidence score from Redwood logs?
03:24 Jared: yes, token-level or response-level confidence is available in the debug pipe; Maya will export the histograms.
03:32 Samir: also curious about the scoring delta — we saw average rubric score drop from 92 to 84 on our sample set after the upgrade.
03:41 Maya: we pulled the evals and it lines up; a tail of prompts dropped. i've got a couple of examples in the shared sheet — link: https://redwood.test/atlas-pocs/prompt-evals (NOTE: internal test link).
03:55 Carlos: on compliance, can you confirm where keys are stored? if we go to Dedicated we want KMS/HSM integration.
04:03 Jared: yes Dedicated supports customer KMS; for hosted we use our managed KMS by default but can integrate with customer-managed keys for enterprise contracts. we'll share the KMS integration doc.
04:17 Samir: ok so immediate ask — can Redwood run the regression test across last three builds and share per-prompt diffs?
04:26 Maya: yes we can run that; timeline about 48 hours to run full suite on the project-scale dataset. we'll prioritize the billing prompt set.
04:36 Lena: please include per-prompt raw outputs and token-level deltas if possible, that helps us triage.
04:42 Maya: can do. also we'll try a quick prompt tuning run — not full finetune, just a small re-ranking prompt edit to bias towards taxonomy answers.
04:53 Samir: is that something we can do in hosted POC or does that require Dedicated?
04:58 Jared: you can do prompt-layer edits in hosted; tuning runs (small adapter-style) would require dedicated capacity for production but can be simulated in hosted for evaluation.
05:10 Carlos: any SLA implications if we run more evals? we might hit rate limits.
05:14 Jared: we can bump quotas for the POC project, AE will patch quotas for the pilot.
05:20 Maya: quick note — we saw one odd transcript where the service replaced 'KV cache' with 'K V cash' in the text, transcription noise, just FYI.
05:30 Lena: ha, that's why we need more robust tokenization checks.
05:33 Samir: ok, next steps?
05:35 Jared: recap: I'll send updated prompt set and the scoring rubric, Maya will export eval runs and run regression across last three builds and share histograms, Maya also to share SOC2 and data flow, Carlos to list outstanding KMS/retention questions, Lena to run internal test harness. We'll aim to reconvene after Atlas uploads regression results.
05:55 Carlos: noted. thanks team.
05:58 Jared: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with links and action items.
06:00 call end

Notes on transcript quality: some speaker labels generic and occasional mis-transcriptions (merchant.com -> merchant.com/policy/xyz) and tokenization errors as noted.

References / artifacts shared during call:
- Prompt eval sheet: https://redwood.test/atlas-pocs/prompt-evals
- Proposed scoring rubric (attachment in follow-up)
- SOC2 + data flow diagram (will be shared by Maya)
